commit.message:
Escape characters outside ASCII in case-entry without literal characters

The pattern ended its range with a literal U+FFFF, an invisible
character in the source. It now names the range with code point
escapes and the `u` flag, and escapes every UTF-16 code unit of each
character it matches, so it prints the same escapes as before.

Point the front-end documents to the links-notation reports

ARCHITECTURE.md said the two repairs keep the runtimes reading the
same forms where links-notation 0.20 does not, but both of its parsers
read `a:` over `b: c` as `(a: c)`; the repairs work around what both
drop, reported as link-foundation/links-notation#313, and around the
last line of spaces the two read differently, reported as
link-foundation/links-notation#312. The shared corpus README names the
nested indented id experiment, and the ledger records the reports, the
new case and limit counts, and the latest comment scan.

Check in both runtimes that only callers select the default type ontology

R129 said the link-cli mapping was not implemented, while R113 already
cites the mirrored interop profile. The new mirrored tests check the
other half of R129: the constructor's definition is the only line of
either runtime's sources that names it, and the evaluator keeps its
stratified universes, answering `Type of Type` only for a source that
declares `(Type: Type Type)`. Adding a call to it in any source file
fails them. recursive-type-ontology.md now calls the ontology a
candidate default construction, and R129 is complete.

Cite the ontology selection tests in R114

R114 stays partial: the new mirrored tests show that no runtime module selects the default type ontology and that the evaluator's universes stay stratified, while universe and soundness contracts declared by a foundation remain open.

Register the public links-notation denial-of-service reports in the ledger

The three denial-of-service findings against links-notation 0.20.0 are now
filed publicly as link-foundation/links-notation#314, #315, and #316 after
the maintainer authorized it: PR comment 5831357798 answered the solver's
question 5831221597. R51 records the three reports with brief descriptions
and notes that the LiNo front end already caps size and depth and reads
quoted references itself; R12 cites their timings alongside the differential
reports #312 and #313. R21, R56, and the ledger header advance the
registered cutoff to comment 5831357798, the latest non-bot requirement,
and R97 records the fresh paginated scan at 2026-09-25T11:55:53Z and notes
that the solver's own PR comments 5831221597 and 5831902886 carry no
requirement. The traceability test enforces the new source.

Report why a linked proof search ended in both runtimes

LinkedProgramRegistry.search runs one saturation for several goals and
reports whether it found every goal, reached a fixed point, spent the
transition bound, or exceeded the fact bound. Goals whose ordered
reduction has no normal form are reported as a rewrite limit, cycle, or
stall instead of rethrown. prove keeps its behavior and now shares the
same saturation in every execution basis.

Let a layer load derived forms through the single linked front end in both runtimes

A layer that declares programs through its own top-level forms can now hand
the registry the forms it derives from the same parse (JS `expandForms`,
Rust `from_rml_expanded`), so the source is read once. The Rust registry also
exposes its program outlines and a classified reduction that reports a rewrite
limit, cycle, or stall as a value, mirroring the JS registry.
Keep the probes that sized S/K witnesses for foundation packages

Add linked foundation packages that witness differing logics, resources, truth policies, and stream typing

Each foundation is a named, versioned package of ordinary linked programs
that play declared roles (axioms, inference, typing, reduction, equality,
truth, proof) with an explicit signature and cycle policy.  Linked
instances import one unchanged theory into a selected foundation, with
optional constant renaming.  The registry ignores the new heads, so the
file already loads as 18 linked programs in both runtimes.

Ask one theory under versioned linked foundations with role-attributed evidence

A linked-foundation packages ordinary linked programs in named roles
(axioms, inference, typing, reduction, equality, truth, proof), depends on
other foundations by version, restricts judgements by signature, and
chooses an inductive or guarded-coinductive cycle policy.  A
linked-instance binds an unchanged theory to one foundation.

FoundationWorkspace answers ground and pattern queries with proved,
refuted, contradictory, unknown, exhausted, and unsupported statuses,
role-attributed proofs, dependency scopes, and incremental revision after
a rule or assumption change.  The module names no logic: the lawn, cafe,
weather, stream, and unseen necessity witnesses are links only, and the
S/K basis stays inside the K0 operations.

Report a search fact without a normal form as a value in Rust

Direct saturation normalizes every input and derived fact with the
ordered rewrites. JavaScript keeps the rewrite-limit, cycle, and stall
classification on the thrown error, but Rust collapsed it into a plain
message. Saturation now carries the classified failure, and
search_or_stop returns it as a ReductionStopped value the way
reduce_or_stop does, so a layer above search can tell a derivation that
ran out of steps from one that cycles. search keeps its error.

The probe in experiments/derived-fact-failure.mjs records the
JavaScript behaviour under both bases.

Ask one theory under versioned linked foundations in Rust

Port the linked foundation workspace to Rust with the same packages,
instances, statuses, reasons, dependencies, and change tracking as the
JavaScript runtime, and mirror its eleven witness tests over
lib/foundations/packages.lino on the direct-structural and closed S/K
bases.

Iterate foundations directly when resolving their dependencies in Rust

Clippy flagged the index loop as needless_range_loop; rustfmt also
re-wrapped the rule-form closure of revise.

Report a spent contraction budget of the closed kernel as exhaustion in both runtimes

A foundation question on the closed S/K basis threw the kernel error once
one kernel call spent the fixed budget of 100 000 000 contractions. The
budget is now a per-call option of the linked-program registry and the
foundation workspace (maxContractions in JavaScript, with_max_contractions
in Rust, each with a getter). A spent budget is classified as the
contraction-limit reason and ends the question exhausted, with the stage
that spent it in the detail.

Execute a replaced linked definition of K1 on the unchanged JavaScript runtime

Swap one links-meta-foundation rule body at a time (repeated-variable
matching, pair substitution, the step after a missed rule, and result
verification) and run the same request on the same runtime. Each
replacement changes the answer while the observed host operations stay
S/K contraction, parsing, and bounds, and the runtime names none of the
constructors those rules use.

With pair substitution mirrored, K1's interpretation of its own rule
follows the new definition and stops agreeing with direct execution,
which still substitutes inside the compiled fixed-point.ski.

Register the full-closure acceptance gate of review 5836717056 in the ledger

R149 records the gate of two comparable minimal meta-foundations with the
seven properties, R150 the D/D' definition-replacement witness (K1 now,
K0 still fixed in the compiled kernel), and R151 the host parser,
elaborator, compiler, and code generation still outside the closure.

Execute a replaced linked definition of K1 on the unchanged Rust runtime

Mirror the JavaScript witness: replacing the matching, substitution,
selection, or verification rule of links-meta-foundation changes the
answer while the host operations stay the same, and replacing K1
substitution leaves K0 substitution in the compiled kernel unchanged.

Load replaceable linked K0 definitions per runtime registry

Select a caller-provided closed Links artifact without rebuilding either runtime. Add a shared nested-substitution replacement witness, isolation and rejection tests, and an explicit remaining trust boundary.

Implement structured RML networks and isolated foundation evidence

Add source-free syntax import/export with bounded expansion, conservative capture-safe identifier rewriting, correct independent guarded truth/refutation search, and linked rational probability/confidence policies. Preserve explicit unsupported language obligations and document remaining semantic closure gaps.

Verified baseline integration: JavaScript 1633 tests and Rust 969 tests; shared corpus and declaration checks pass. Added adversarial expansion tests accompany the final structure safety repair.

Deliver linked proofs, isolated packages, translations and safe build lifecycle

Add bounded inductive certificate verification with independent replay, version-private foundation packages, strict typed-link archives, all twelve portable-natural translation paths with native observations, and direct linked-source execution controls.

Install repository-scoped cache lifecycle and composed hooks, protect source/evidence/worktrees, coordinate process-realm leases, and record measured clean rebuilds. Preserve the existing completion-check entry point pending the separate source-inventory acceptance checkpoint.

This is verified implementation progress in issue 183; full-language, whole-corpus and minimal-foundation closure remain open.
